justification_text:
My point estimates reflect a relatively stable near-term outlook with modest upward drift over longer horizons. At the one-day horizon, the estimate of 574 is essentially anchored to the most recent observed value, with very little expected movement given typical daily continuity and mean-reversion tendencies in most time series of this kind. At the one-week horizon, the slight uptick to 578 reflects a small positive trend component built into the baseline, acknowledging that short-term momentum often persists modestly. By one month, the estimate rises further to 585, incorporating a gradual drift assumption while remaining fairly conservative — I did not want to extrapolate aggressively without stronger directional signals in the data.

The confidence interval widths grow appropriately with the forecast horizon, reflecting the compounding of uncertainty over time. At one day, the 90% interval of 556–592 is relatively tight because daily fluctuations tend to be small and predictable. By one week, the interval widens to 545–612, capturing the accumulation of day-to-day variability and the possibility that any single unusual day could shift the trajectory. At one month, the interval of 520–650 is substantially wider, reflecting genuine uncertainty about structural shifts, external shocks, or trend reversals that are difficult to anticipate at that distance.

Several factors influenced my uncertainty assumptions beyond simple variance scaling. Seasonal patterns, if present, could introduce systematic deviations that my baseline model does not fully capture. Additionally, any underlying cyclical or policy-driven dynamics that operate on weekly or monthly timescales could cause the realized outcome to cluster toward one end of the interval rather than the center.

Specific risks that could push outcomes outside my stated intervals include sudden structural breaks — for example, a major external shock, policy announcement, or data revision that resets the level of the series entirely. On the upside, a sustained acceleration in whatever underlying process generates these values could push the one-month outcome well above 650. On the downside, a sharp reversal or negative shock could bring the value below 520. These tail events are by definition low-probability but not negligible, and they represent the primary reason I kept my intervals relatively wide at the monthly horizon despite the stable short-term picture.
